:::{#thm-taylor-1d}
#### Taylor's theorem with a second-order remainder

Let $a < b$, and let $g$ be a real-valued function on $[a, b]$
whose derivative $g'$ is [continuous](calculus.qmd#def-continuous) on $[a, b]$
and whose [second derivative](calculus.qmd#def-second-derivative) $g''$ exists at every point of $(a, b)$.
Then there is a $\midpt \in (a, b)$ with

$$
g(b) = g(a) + g'(a)\,(b - a) + \frac{1}{2}\,g''(\midpt)\,(b - a)^2.
$$

:::

This theorem is the case $n = 2$ of [@rudin1976principles, Theorem 5.15];
its proof uses the mean value theorem, which these notes do not develop.

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-taylor-1d}
#### The remainder point for $e^x$

Take $g(x) = e^x$ on $[0, 1]$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
g' &= g'' \\
&= g.
\end{aligned}
$$

@thm-taylor-1d says $e = 1 + 1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,e^{\midpt}$ for some $\midpt \in (0, 1)$.
Solving,

$$
\begin{aligned}
e^{\midpt} &= 2 (e - 2) \\
&\approx 2 \times 0.71828 \\
&= 1.43656,
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\midpt = \log 1.43656 \approx 0.362$ ([natural logarithm](algebra.qmd#def-natural-log)), which is in $(0, 1)$.

:::
